Detail

12.9 plates/min. It falls 15.31 -> 10.28 -> 7.3 -> 5.0 and then holds for three consecutive cycles to the centisecond. The run's last cycle came back at 7.07 s - a vision outlier, 2.98 s of vision wait against a 0.58 s norm - so 4.66 s is the demonstrated floor of this run, not a rate it held to the end.

column1: Almost half the cycle is one opaque number
column3: place+return is 2.13 s of 4.66 s (46%) and contains eight distinct things, including a second AperaPartsFound() vision round-trip that is NOT in the vision-wait timer. Splitting it is the highest-information edit available and it changes no behaviour.

column1: Magnet dwell is 1.35 s - 29% of the cycle
column3: 0.85 s of it appears on every single cycle to the centisecond, zero variance across 17 cycles, which confirms it is fixed dwell with no motion in it. Reducing it cannot throw a plate. How short the coil can go is a bench measurement, not something the source can settle.

column1: The retreat timer is misleading, not free
column3: SegRetreat reads 0.00 because movej only queues motion and returns; there is no waitEndMove() after apera_follow_trajectory, so the timer measures queue time. Anyone reading the Cycle Timing page today would conclude the retreat costs nothing.

column1: The early trigger reaches about 3% of picks
column3: It fires only on a last-part belt kick: 0 of 17 in this run, 5 of 145 in the snapshot. It worked 5 of 5 with no APERA error. Extending it to every pick would hide the 0.59 s vision wait behind the place motion on all picks - the vision wait is 12.5% of the steady-state cycle and 13.9% of the whole-run mean, so that is the size of the prize. Higher risk, so it belongs on its own.

column1: Only the drop-station camera cube is ever occupied
column3: nFovHitStart 0, nFovHitEnd 15 of 145. The conveyor camera - the only one that can occlude the pick pipeline - was never blocked, which is what made gating the early trigger on _bStartFoV alone safe.

Phase timers account for 99.6% of the cycle, with 0.01-0.03 s unaccounted on 16 of 17 cycles (0.00 on one of them). There is no hidden dwell. The one exception is cycle 2, at 3.03 s unaccounted - and that is the single cycle where nBranchBPasses incremented.

column1: 1. Make both magnet dwells tunable, then sweep
column3: 29% of the cycle, no path or acceleration change. Split nEMH_gripperDelay into ON/OFF - it is one number used for both pulses - and make tkCycle's hard-coded delay(0.35) a public nGripSettle. GATED on a bench test of the coil's make and break time.
Pure instrumentation, zero risk. 46% of the cycle is currently one number.
A timer reading zero on a phase that clearly takes time is worse than no timer.

column1: 4. Consider the early trigger on every pick
column3: Worth about 12-14%. Higher risk - it is the moving-robot capture - so do it after 1-3 and alone, so it can be judged alone.
Not where the time is. The motion phases total about 1.1 s against 1.35 s of pure dwell. Dwell first, and only then with the magnet hold margin measured.

Four lines per pick at 4.7 s is roughly 4 MB/day into user.log. Check the CS9's rotation size before a long run so the CSV does not evict the diagnostics it sits alongside. If it does, emit lines C and D every Nth cycle - the counters are cumulative, so they lose nothing by being sampled.
